title: ptc-tag-team-tournament
label: Shane Stone & The Bum Boozler

won.source: User-attested: a contributor's own account of having wrestled and won it, corroborated on the alliance's own re-hosted forum — the champions' own tag-title defence of 28 September 2003 (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/tag-titles-match/266/1), a beaten opponent's own recollection of losing to them twice in it (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/next-tag-match/427/25), the same thread's own reply from one of the winners (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/next-tag-match/427/28), and a third poster's “I still owe you twice for the tag team tournament in the old PTC” (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/next-tag-match/427/23).

how: Won as the pairing the alliance billed “Homophobic” — one half of The Phenomenons with a partner from outside that team, never The Phenomenons themselves. The final is undated in what survives; the earliest surviving word of the win is the pair's own defence of the PTC World Tag Team Championship on 28 September 2003, where the ring announcer introduces “the current PTC World Tag Team Champions Homophobic”. A beaten opponent's own handler recounts the tournament in the alliance's own forum — “I was in the PTC TTT tournament with my friend Zero as Banned and Exiled. We lost to you… Later I teamed with Sin as a replacement for his partner and faced you in the next round of the tournament… So I lost to you twice in one tournament from two partner no shows” — and one of the winners answers him in the same thread: “we beat YOU twice… accept it.”

conflict.reading_a: The pairing billed “Homophobic” — Shane Stone and The Bum Boozler — won it: a contributor's own attested account, the pair billed as the alliance's reigning World Tag Team Champions on 28 September 2003, and a beaten opponent and a third poster both crediting that team with beating them twice in the one tournament.
conflict.reading_b: PTCpedia's own “Banned & Exiled~!” article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-banned-exiled.html) instead names the winners as The Phenomenons, and calls the event “the first and only Primetime Central Tag Team tournament”. The same article's account of the losing side is contradicted in detail by that side's own handler, who names a different first partner and a different sequence, and the alliance's own board carries a later tag-team tournament final of April 2004, so “first and only” is not supported either. Recorded as that article's own claim, not settled.

title: ptc-cruiserweight-tournament
label: Seymour Almasy

won.source: The tournament's own news, posted by Argyle: "Semi Final Results~!" (11 May 2004: "In a close matchup, Seymour Almasy defeated Syko Arsonist, two votes to one") and "Drumroll..... and the winner is...." (26 May 2004: "Winner of the First Annual PTC Cruiserweight Tournament (2004) is... Seymour Almasy, 2 votes to 1.") (/promotions/ptc/news/semi-final-results-2004-05-11.html; /promotions/ptc/news/drumroll-and-the-winner-is-2004-05-26.html); the CW site's own bracket rows (Argyle's database, accession 0159: the semi-final and the final, each 2 votes to 1, "Three judges. The result was posted on 26 May 2004."); and PTCpedia's own PTC Cruiserweight Tournament article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-cruiserweight-tournament.html, captured 7 Mar 2008), whose final-four paragraph has Almasy prevail over Syko Arsonist and then, in the final, over Karina Wolfenden.

how: CW1. Almasy beat Karina Wolfenden in the final, two votes to one from three judges, the result posted on 26 May 2004. The final four were Almasy, Syko Arsonist, Karina Wolfenden and Ethan Knight: Almasy beat Syko Arsonist in the semi-finals, also two votes to one, and Wolfenden beat Ethan Knight. Brackets posted 22 March 2004 by Tournament Director Argyle.

title: ptc-cruiserweight-tournament
label: CK

won.source: PTCpedia's own PTC Cruiserweight Tournament article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-cruiserweight-tournament.html, captured 7 Mar 2008). This document carries 1 redaction, per the privacy rule. The CW2 texts cited are the CW tournaments' own backstage database (accession 0159): the CW2 bracket news (8620), the final's bracket row, and the winner's roleplays 35281, 35307 and 35313.

how: CW2. XUW's own `ck`, billed "Cereal Killer" in that fed's own text: its Television and Cruiserweight Champion, Cruiserweight Champion from 31 Jan 2002 and still champion at the end of XUW's surviving record. The CW2 bracket news (8620) and the final row tag the winner XUW, and his own CW2 roleplays tell XUW's Cereal Killer: 35281 (15 Apr 2005) the Army of Darkness formed with Jack "The Ripper" Nobbledy at Mayhem, "the first ever weekly televised show", their XUW Tag Titles, his XUW Cruiserweight Title, and the word that XUW "still think you're the Cruiserweight Champion"; 35307 (30 Apr 2005) "the XUW entrant in PTC's second annual cruiserweight tournament"; 35313 (14 May 2005) "the XUW entrant to the tournament", still drawing "that paycheck from XUW".
